title: The Card Index and the Bank: from West Fifty-Fourth Street to Hudson Pines
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The House on West Fifty-Fourth Street

stops.name: 10 West 54th Street, the birth of the fifth son
stops.date_confidence: attested. Wikipedia and the Rockefeller Archive Center agree on 12 June 1915 and on the address. The coordinate is corrected northward from a dossier value of 40.7605, which falls below West 53rd Street; 10 West 54th fronted the north side of West 54th, and the point must sit north of MoMA at 40.7617 and of the sculpture garden at 40.7614, not south of both.
stops.campa: The sixth child and fifth son of John D. Rockefeller Jr. and Abby Aldrich Rockefeller is born in the family house at 10 West Fifty-Fourth Street, a few doors along the block from the brownstone at number 4 where his grandfather John D. Rockefeller Sr. keeps his ledgers. The date is the twelfth of June 1915. The whole street belongs, in effect, to one family. The house comes down in 1937, and a sculpture garden named for his mother is laid out over its footprint.
suggested_refs: The Rockefeller houses on the north side of West 54th Street, demolished 1937 for the MoMA sculpture garden site
sources: Rockefeller Archive Center, biographical record, rockarch.org
john_d_rockefeller_sr.journey.json, stop '4 West 54th Street, the brownstone off Fifth Avenue'

stops.name: The Lincoln School, twelve years of Dewey's pedagogy
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the twelve years and the 1932 graduation, per the Rockefeller Archive Center. Month and day of first enrollment are not recorded and default to September for ordering.
stops.campa: He is sent to the Lincoln School of Teachers College at Columbia, an experimental school his father's money built and John Dewey's pedagogy shaped, and he stays twelve years. There is no rote drill and no Latin; there are field trips, shop work, cooking, and a curriculum written as an argument about what American schooling ought to be. Abraham Flexner drew up the plan and the General Education Board paid for it. The fifth son of the family does his arithmetic beside the children of Columbia faculty. He graduates in 1932.
suggested_refs: Abraham Flexner's founding plan for the Lincoln School of Teachers College, financed by the General Education Board
sources: Rockefeller Archive Center, biographical record, rockarch.org

stops.name: Pocantico Hills, the estate above the Hudson
stops.date_confidence: traditional. The date is an ordering device for a childhood, not an event. The pin is the canonical Pocantico Hills point already used for his grandfather. A dossier claim that he grew up at Kykuit is corrected here: Rockefeller's own Memoirs, quoted in Wikipedia's Pocantico Hills article, say 'Grandfather occupied Kykuit from 1912 until his death in 1937, and then Mother and Father moved into it.' The visitors he recalls, George C. Marshall, Richard E. Byrd, Charles Lindbergh, rest on his own later recollection and are not independently documented; treat as [R].
stops.campa: Weekends and holidays are spent on the family land above the Hudson at Pocantico Hills, thousands of acres of woods, carriage roads and cut stone. Kykuit at the top of the rise is his grandfather's house; the old man occupies it from 1912 until his death in 1937, and the boy's own household lives elsewhere on the estate. The visitors he will remember from these years are George C. Marshall, Richard E. Byrd and Charles Lindbergh. Nothing outside his own later account records that any of them were there.
suggested_refs: Kykuit, National Historic Landmark, and the surrounding Pocantico estate of John D. Rockefeller Jr.
sources: john_d_rockefeller_sr.journey.json, stop 'Pocantico Hills, buying the ridge above the Hudson'

stops.name: Seal Harbor, the summers at The Eyrie
stops.date_confidence: attested as a childhood pattern by the Rockefeller Archive Center biographical record; the specific year and month are an ordering device only.
stops.campa: Summers are spent at The Eyrie, the Rockefeller house at Seal Harbor on Mount Desert Island in Maine. The household travels with its staff; the grounds are watched by men paid to watch them; charitable giving is a prescribed duty set out for the children as an obligation attached to the money rather than an impulse of the heart. He is ten years old, the youngest of the six children and the last of them born in the house on West Fifty-Fourth Street.
suggested_refs: The Eyrie, Seal Harbor, the Rockefeller summer house on Mount Desert Island
sources: Rockefeller Archive Center, biographical record, rockarch.org

stops.name: Harvard College, economics in the pit of the Depression
stops.date_confidence: attested: entered 1932, graduated cum laude 1936 with a B.S. in economics. Month of matriculation defaults to September. The Schumpeter contact is given by the Rockefeller Archive Center record as exposure to his thought rather than as documented tutelage; treat that clause as [R].
stops.campa: He enters Harvard in 1932 and reads economics in the pit of the Depression, when the question in front of the discipline is why capital and labour sit idle while people go hungry. Joseph Schumpeter's arguments are in the air at Cambridge in those years, and the problem of how institutions might mobilize unused resources takes hold of him. He graduates cum laude in 1936 with a B.S. Seventy-two years later he will give the college a hundred million dollars, earmarked for undergraduates going abroad and for the arts.
suggested_refs: Harvard College class of 1936; the 2008 Rockefeller gift for undergraduate international experience and the arts
sources: Rockefeller Archive Center, biographical record, rockarch.org

stops.name: The London School of Economics, Hayek against the underconsumptionists
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1937 by Wikipedia's chronology and by the LSE history blog, which states he arrived 'in the fall of 1937.' A dossier geography entry dating the year 1936-1937 is one year early and is corrected here. Month defaults to October for the Michaelmas term.
stops.campa: He crosses to London in the autumn and reads economics at the London School of Economics on Houghton Street. Friedrich Hayek is there, arguing against the underconsumptionists, and the argument lodges: Rockefeller prepares work criticizing underconsumption theory and carries the question home with him. He does not become a doctrinaire Austrian. He stays one academic year and goes back across the Atlantic to take a doctorate at Chicago on the question of idle resources.
suggested_refs: LSE History blog, 'LSE: Rockefeller's baby,' on the Rockefeller funding of the School and on his year there
sources: Rockefeller Archive Center, biographical record, rockarch.org

stops.name: The University of Chicago, Unused Resources and Economic Waste
stops.date_confidence: attested: Ph.D. in economics, 1940, dissertation 'Unused Resources and Economic Waste.' Month defaults to June for the degree year. The pin is the canonical University of Chicago point already carried in his grandfather's file.
stops.campa: He takes his doctorate at the University of Chicago with a dissertation titled 'Unused Resources and Economic Waste,' a study of idle labour and idle capital under depression conditions, later issued in book form by the university press. The subject is the one he has carried since Harvard and London: not scarcity but waste. He is twenty-five, and it is the last piece of academic work he will produce. He goes on using its vocabulary for sixty years.
suggested_refs: David Rockefeller, Unused Resources and Economic Waste (University of Chicago Press, 1941)
sources: Rockefeller Archive Center, biographical record, rockarch.org

stops.name: Bedford, the marriage to Margaret McGrath
stops.date_confidence: date attested by the Rockefeller Archive Center: 'Married Margaret McGrath on September 7, 1940.' The church, St. Matthew's Episcopal at Bedford, appears only in the research dossier and in neither RAC nor Wikipedia; the coordinate therefore rests on a single unverified locality claim. A dossier entry naming the bride 'Margaret McGrath Dulany' fused her with their daughter Peggy Dulany and is corrected here.
stops.campa: He marries Margaret McGrath, called Peggy, on the seventh of September in Westchester County. He is twenty-five and has just finished the doctorate. The marriage runs fifty-five years, until her death in 1996, and produces six children, among them a daughter also called Peggy. Margaret Rockefeller becomes a working conservationist and a collector alongside her husband. Which church at Bedford held the ceremony is claimed in one place and confirmed in none.
suggested_refs: Rockefeller Archive Center record of the marriage, 7 September 1940
sources: Rockefeller Archive Center, biographical record, rockarch.org

stops.name: New York City Hall, secretary to La Guardia
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1940-1941 by Wikipedia and the Rockefeller Archive Center; exact start month not recorded and defaulted to October to sit after the September marriage. Pin is the canonical New York City point.
stops.campa: He goes to work at City Hall as secretary to Mayor Fiorello La Guardia. The office is a fire hose: housing complaints, transit deficits, relief rolls, and the ethnic arithmetic of the five boroughs. For a year and more the grandson of Standard Oil sits at the elbow of a mayor who made his career denouncing that kind of money, and learns how a municipal administration actually moves. He is twenty-five, and the job lasts a little over a year. It is the only public office he will ever hold.
suggested_refs: The La Guardia administration papers, City of New York, 1940-1941
sources: Rockefeller Archive Center, biographical record, rockarch.org

stops.name: Fort Jay, Governors Island, enlisting as a private
stops.date_confidence: attested by Wikipedia to 1 May 1942 at Fort Jay. His stated refusal of a special commission comes from the Rockefeller Archive Center record and from a CIA Studies in Intelligence article by David Robarge cited in the dossier; cia.gov returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch, so the CIA study is used as reported by convergent secondary accounts and not as a page anyone here loaded.
stops.campa: He enlists as a private at Fort Jay on Governors Island on the first of May, turning aside the efforts made on his behalf to secure a direct commission. He is twenty-six, married, holds a doctorate, and is the son of the wealthiest family in America, and he goes in at the bottom rank the army has. He does not want a favour attached to his name in a war other men are being drafted into. Basic training follows, with the ordinary intake, in the ordinary way.
suggested_refs: David Robarge, 'David Rockefeller's Wartime Intelligence Service,' CIA Studies in Intelligence (fetch blocked, HTTP 403)
sources: Rockefeller Archive Center, biographical record, rockarch.org

stops.name: Fort Belvoir, Officer Candidate School
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1943 by Wikipedia; the month is not recorded in any source reached and defaults to January. The syllabus detail (demolition, rigging, camouflage, forced marches) comes from RAC chronology material consistent with the Robarge CIA study, which could not be fetched directly.
stops.campa: He is sent to Officer Candidate School at Fort Belvoir on the Potomac: demolition, rigging, camouflage, forced marches under a pack. He comes out a second lieutenant, and the assignment that follows is intelligence, on the strength of the French he learned as a boy. The engineering syllabus is not what the army will end up using him for. What the months at Belvoir amount to is a man approaching thirty being shouted at in a field in Virginia by men who do not know his name.
suggested_refs: The U.S. Army Engineer School at Fort Belvoir, wartime officer candidate program

stops.name: Camp Ritchie, the school for interrogators
stops.date_confidence: [R]. The training is attested by Wikipedia; the detail rests on the Robarge CIA study, cia.gov, which returned HTTP 403 and was not loaded here. Month is an ordering default. The coordinate is corrected: a dossier value of 39.6551, -77.4886 points at open country some 5.7 km from the post. Wikipedia's 'Fort Ritchie' gives 39.7053, -77.4960, at Cascade, Maryland. The wartime name Camp Ritchie is correct for 1926-1951.
stops.campa: At Camp Ritchie in the Maryland hills he trains in battlefield intelligence: map reading, terrain reconnaissance, order of battle, and the interrogation of prisoners. The camp is turning out the men later called the Ritchie Boys, a great many of them German and Austrian refugees whose value to the army is their mother tongue. Rockefeller's language is French and his asset is a European address book inherited rather than earned. He is at Ritchie in the spring of 1943 and in North Africa by August.
suggested_refs: The Military Intelligence Training Center at Camp Ritchie, Maryland, 1942-1946
sources: David Robarge, CIA Studies in Intelligence (cited, not fetched)

stops.name: Algiers, the Joint Intelligence Collection Agency
stops.date_confidence: [R]. Wikipedia places the Algiers assignment in 1943 and gives the roughly 10,000 miles across Algeria, Morocco and Tunisia; the Vanier letter of introduction and the JICA attachment come from the Robarge CIA study, not fetched (HTTP 403). Pin is the canonical Algiers point.
stops.campa: He reaches Allied intelligence headquarters in Algiers in August and is put to the Joint Intelligence Collection Agency, reporting on the factions inside French North Africa: Gaullists, Giraudists, Vichy holdouts, settlers, and the Arab and Berber population none of them speaks for. He carries letters of introduction his family's name has produced, among them one to the Canadian general Georges Vanier, and he uses them. Over the assignment he covers something like ten thousand miles of Algeria, Morocco and Tunisia.
suggested_refs: The Joint Intelligence Collection Agency, North African theatre, 1943-1944
sources: David Robarge, CIA Studies in Intelligence (cited, not fetched)

stops.name: Cairo, the Mediterranean circuit
stops.date_confidence: [R] and thin. The Cairo and Istanbul visits appear only in the CIA-study-derived account in the research dossier; no page confirming them was reachable. Date is an ordering default within the stated 1943-1944 range. Pin is the canonical Cairo point.
stops.campa: The circuit run out of Algiers reaches Cairo, and beyond it Istanbul, the two great listening posts of the eastern war. He is twenty-eight and has been in uniform for eighteen months. The work is political intelligence: contacts, names and dispositions collected to be filed and cross-referenced later, by the method he will keep for forty years, which is to go and see the person yourself and write it down afterward. What he did in either city the record does not describe in any detail.
suggested_refs: Allied intelligence liaison in Cairo and Istanbul, 1943-1944
sources: David Robarge, CIA Studies in Intelligence, as summarized in the research dossier (cia.gov fetch returned HTTP 403)

stops.name: Lyon, T Force through liberated France
stops.date_confidence: [R]. The T Force travels through Lyon, Marseille, Bordeaux and Biarritz are given only by the CIA-study-derived account in the dossier, which could not be fetched. The dossier itself dates them loosely to October-December 1944; October is used here to order the segment. Pins for Lyon, Marseille and Bordeaux match canonical atlas points.
stops.campa: Attached to T Force, he travels alone through a France liberated a few weeks earlier: from Lyon down the Rhone to Marseille, west to Bordeaux, and on to Biarritz on the Basque coast. He reports on retreating German units, on the Resistance factions now competing for local power, on industrial capacity and the condition of the ports, and on the Spanish Republican exiles waiting out Franco in the southwest. The countryside is armed and barely policed. He is a lieutenant with a car, a notebook and no escort.
suggested_refs: T Force political and economic intelligence collection in southern France, autumn 1944
sources: David Robarge, CIA Studies in Intelligence, as summarized in the research dossier (cia.gov fetch returned HTTP 403)

stops.name: Paris, the assistant military attache and the Intelligence Library
stops.date_confidence: the 6 March 1945 appointment as assistant military attache in Paris is attested by Wikipedia. The coded card index called the Intelligence Library comes from the Robarge CIA study and from Memoirs; the CIA page returned HTTP 403 and the memoir text was not re-checked at this passage. Pin is the canonical Paris point (48.8566, 2.3522) inherited from the existing atlas files.
stops.campa: On the sixth of March he becomes assistant military attache in Paris and builds a political and economic intelligence unit out of nothing. Its heart is a card index he designs himself, cross-referenced by person, subject and place, and calls the Intelligence Library. From Paris he makes reporting trips into Belgium, Germany, Austria and Czechoslovakia. He leaves active duty a captain, with the Legion of Merit and the French Legion of Honour, and with the index. The card file goes with him into banking.
suggested_refs: The 'Intelligence Library' card index, prototype of the Rockefeller contact file at Chase
sources: David Robarge, CIA Studies in Intelligence (cited, not fetched)

stops.name: Dachau, the camp after the liberation
stops.date_confidence: [R]. The Dachau and Prague visits come from the CIA-study-derived account in the dossier and were not independently confirmed. The month is an ordering default: Dachau was liberated 29 April 1945. Coordinate corrected from a dossier value of 48.2649, 11.4681, roughly 560 m south of the memorial site, to approximately 48.2699, 11.4665.
stops.campa: His reporting circuit through occupied Germany brings him to Dachau, north-west of Munich, after the camp's liberation, and afterward to Prague. The camp was liberated on the twenty-ninth of April, days before the German surrender. He is twenty-nine, a captain of intelligence attached to an embassy, one of the many men in uniform who walk into one of these places in the spring of 1945 and afterwards go home to long ordinary lives. He records the visit and does not enlarge on it.
suggested_refs: The Dachau concentration camp memorial site, liberated 29 April 1945
sources: David Robarge, CIA Studies in Intelligence, as summarized in the research dossier (cia.gov fetch returned HTTP 403)

segments.name: The Foreign Department and the Downtown

stops.name: 18 Pine Street, the foreign department
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1946 by Wikipedia and the Rockefeller Archive Center; month not recorded, defaulted to January. Coordinate corrected eastward from a dossier value of -74.0113, which lands near Broadway and Trinity Church; Chase National Bank's head office stood at 18 Pine Street, approximately 40.7075, -74.0089.
stops.campa: He joins Chase National Bank at 18 Pine Street as an assistant manager in the foreign department, the lowest officer's rung, at an institution his uncle Winthrop Aldrich chairs. Thirty-five years of his life begin here. The foreign department in 1946 is a small thing: correspondent relationships, letters of credit, a handful of overseas branches left standing after the war. When he leaves the bank in 1981 it has offices on every inhabited continent.
suggested_refs: Chase National Bank head office, 18 Pine Street, Manhattan
sources: Rockefeller Archive Center, biographical record, rockarch.org

stops.name: The Museum of Modern Art, his mother's seat and the garden on the house's ground
stops.date_confidence: trustee from 1948 attested. The office sequence is corrected against Wikipedia's MoMA article: he took the presidency in 1958 when Nelson was elected governor, and was chairman 1962-1972 and 1987-1993. A dossier entry giving '1958-59' as a chairmanship conflates the presidency with the chair. The garden was built spring 1952 to April 1953, designed by Philip Johnson. Month of the 1948 trusteeship not recorded. Pin is the canonical West 54th Street block point.
stops.campa: His mother dies and he takes her seat on the board of the Museum of Modern Art, the museum she helped found and filled with pictures her husband disliked. He is trustee from 1948, president from 1958 when Nelson goes to Albany as governor, chairman from 1962. In 1952 he engages Philip Johnson to lay out a garden on the ground of the demolished house where he was born, and names it for her. Eighteen years before that, his brother Nelson had ordered Diego Rivera's Rockefeller Center mural destroyed, after the painter refused to remove Lenin's face from it.
suggested_refs: The Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Sculpture Garden, designed by Philip Johnson, built 1952-1953
MoMA archival finding aid, moma.org/docs/learn/archives/ROCKEFELLER_FINAL_ACCESS.pdf
sources: Rockefeller Archive Center, biographical record, rockarch.org
diego_rivera.journey.json, the Rockefeller Center mural stops

stops.name: The Harold Pratt House, the Council on Foreign Relations board
stops.date_confidence: the 1949 board election is attested by Wikipedia; the chairmanship 1970-1985 is given in the dossier and corroborated by the allen_dulles atlas file's account of the Council. Month not recorded, defaulted to January. The Pratt House coordinate is the Council's 58 East 68th Street address; the Council occupied 45 East 65th Street before 1945, which is the address the Dulles file carries for the earlier period.
stops.campa: He joins the board of directors of the Council on Foreign Relations at the Harold Pratt House on the Upper East Side. Allen Dulles, president of the Council since 1946 and head of the Central Intelligence Agency within four years, sits at the same table. Rockefeller will stay on that board for thirty-six years and chair it from 1970 to 1985. He is thirty-four, and he holds the Council seat, the bank job and the museum trusteeship at once. He will hold all three for the next twenty years.
suggested_refs: The Harold Pratt House, 58 East 68th Street, seat of the Council on Foreign Relations since 1945
sources: allen_dulles.journey.json, the Council on Foreign Relations stops

stops.name: One Chase Manhattan Plaza, the tower and the association
stops.date_confidence: the Downtown-Lower Manhattan Association was organized in 1958 and chaired by him to 1975 (attested, Chase corporate history). The world trade centre clause is weakly sourced: the dossier cited a 1980 Time archive piece, time.com/archive/6856006, which was fetched and contains no mention of the World Trade Center, Radio Row, the Port Authority or the D-LMA. The advocacy is general knowledge in the literature but no page confirming it was loaded for this file. Treat that final sentence as [R].
stops.campa: He founds the Downtown-Lower Manhattan Association and chairs it until 1975, on the argument that the financial district will empty into midtown unless somebody anchors it. The anchor he builds is Chase's own new headquarters, sixty storeys of aluminium and glass on a plaza south of Liberty Street, the first modern tower below Wall Street. He is vice chairman of the bank when he pushes it through and president by the time it opens. The association's other proposal, a world trade centre on the Hudson terminal ground, will take the Port Authority another decade. The electronics dealers of Radio Row lose their street to it.
suggested_refs: The Downtown-Lower Manhattan Association records, 1958-1975
Radio Row, Cortlandt Street, condemned for the World Trade Center site
sources: Chase corporate history as summarized in encyclopedic biography of David Rockefeller
Euromoney, 'The bankers that define the decades: David Rockefeller'

stops.name: York Avenue, the institute becomes a university
stops.date_confidence: attested: trustee from 1940, chair from 1950, reorganization as a degree-granting university in 1965, chair to 1975. Month not recorded. Coordinate matches Wikipedia's Rockefeller University point to the digit. A dossier claim that his final 2010 pledge funded the campus expansion over the FDR Drive is wrong on the expansion, which is the Stavros Niarchos Foundation-David Rockefeller River Campus completed in 2019, and the 2010 pledge itself could not be confirmed in any source reached; it is therefore not carried here.
stops.campa: The Rockefeller Institute for Medical Research on York Avenue, founded by his grandfather in 1901 to fight hookworm and yellow fever, is reorganized as a degree-granting institution and renamed Rockefeller University. Its laboratories now award doctorates in their own name. He has been a trustee since 1940 and chairman since 1950; he holds the chair until 1975 and stays on the board for the rest of his life, seventy-six years of trusteeship at one institution.
suggested_refs: The 1965 charter amendment converting the Rockefeller Institute into Rockefeller University

stops.name: One Chase Manhattan Plaza, chairman and chief executive
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1969 by Wikipedia. Note a live inconsistency in the sources for the earlier promotion: Wikipedia's summary dates his presidency of Chase to 1960, other institutional histories to 1961. That contradiction is recorded, not resolved. Month of the 1969 elevation not recorded.
stops.campa: He becomes chairman and chief executive of Chase Manhattan. What he does with the office is not conventional banking: he travels. Heads of state, finance ministers, central bankers, dictators and their treasurers, every one of them entered on the cards. The bank's business follows the itinerary, or is understood to. Inside Chase there is a standing complaint, printed eventually in Time, that the chairman is abroad building a reputation as a world statesman while the operations floor in New York cannot reconcile its own accounts.
suggested_refs: Time, 'Business: The Change at David's Bank,' 1 September 1980

stops.name: New York, the Business Group for Latin America
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1963 that he organized the Business Group for Latin America at President Kennedy's request, and that it became the Council for Latin America and then the Council of the Americas. Month not recorded. The Cuban framing is [R]: the fidel_castro atlas file records the 1961 Punta del Este refusal and the nationalizations that followed but does not name Chase, and no source reached here confirms the seizure of Chase's Havana branches specifically. Pin is the canonical New York City point.
stops.campa: President Kennedy asks him to organize American business behind the Alliance for Progress, and he forms the Business Group for Latin America, later the Council for Latin America and then the Council of the Americas. Rockefeller will sit on hemispheric business councils for the next forty years. The occasion is Cuba: Fidel Castro's government has nationalized the foreign banks, and Washington wants private capital moving south before the example spreads any further.
suggested_refs: The Council of the Americas, successor to the Business Group for Latin America (1963)
sources: fidel_castro.journey.json, the Punta del Este stop

stops.name: Singapore, a country of eight hundred million people
stops.date_confidence: the quoted phrases and the Singapore press conference are attested in Rockefeller's own Memoirs, chapter 'Penetrating the Bamboo Curtain,' dated there to 1970. Month and day are not given and default to January. The Singapore coordinate is the city point, not a specific venue, which is not recorded.
stops.campa: At a Chase press conference in Singapore he calls the relaxation of American trade restrictions on the People's Republic a logical and good step toward seeking some sort of contact. Richard Nixon will not go to Peking for another eighteen months, and Chase's correspondent relationship with the Bank of China follows within three years. The banker is out ahead of the government, which is the position he prefers. What he says in the room is that it is no longer possible 'to act as if a country of 800 million people did not exist.'
stops.quote: to act as if a country of 800 million people did not exist
stops.quote_source: David Rockefeller at a Chase press conference in Singapore, 1970, quoted in his Memoirs (Random House, 2002), chapter 'Penetrating the Bamboo Curtain'
suggested_refs: Memoirs, chapter 'Penetrating the Bamboo Curtain,' on the 1970 Singapore press conference

stops.name: Montreal, the commission proposed
stops.date_confidence: attested to March 1972 by Memoirs, which quotes him from a series of Chase international investment forums held at Montreal, London, Brussels and Paris. Which city carried which sentence is not distinguished in the source; Montreal is used as the pin for the series. Day not recorded.
stops.campa: Speaking at Chase investment forums in Montreal, London, Brussels and Paris that March, he proposes a private body joining North America, Western Europe and Japan on trade and investment, environmental problems, the control of crime and drugs, population control, and assistance to developing nations. Within sixteen months the Trilateral Commission exists, with Zbigniew Brzezinski directing it. Bilderberg, the older table, has declined to admit the Japanese.
stops.quote: international commission for peace and prosperity
stops.quote_source: David Rockefeller, Chase international investment forum speeches, March 1972, quoted in his Memoirs (Random House, 2002), chapter on the Trilateral Commission
suggested_refs: Memoirs, the Trilateral Commission chapter, on the March 1972 forum speeches

stops.name: Moscow, the representative office and the long Soviet line
stops.date_confidence: the 1973 Moscow representative office, first American banking presence there since the 1920s, is [R]: the dossier attributes it to Rockefeller Archive Center chronology and it was not independently re-fetched. The 1964 Khrushchev meeting is [R] and needs a genuine source: the dossier cited the 1980 Time archive piece, which was fetched and contains no mention of Khrushchev. The Gorbachev exchange is attested verbatim in Memoirs chapter 17, 'Engaging the Soviets,' and took place at the Soviet embassy in Washington in December 1987, not in Moscow. Month here is an ordering default.
stops.campa: Chase opens a representative office in Moscow, the first American bank present in the Soviet capital since the 1920s. Rockefeller has been coming here since 1964, when an unofficial conference put him in a room with Nikita Khrushchev. He is a private banker who keeps a line open across the Cold War frontier because he has decided that lines should be open. The line runs to the end. In December 1987, at a reception in the Soviet embassy in Washington, he asks Mikhail Gorbachev whether the rouble can be made convertible.
stops.quote: We are studying this issue and will be making some important decisions before long.
stops.quote_source: Mikhail Gorbachev to David Rockefeller, reception at the Soviet embassy, Washington, D.C., December 1987, quoted in Memoirs (Random House, 2002), chapter 17, 'Engaging the Soviets'
suggested_refs: The Chase Manhattan representative office, Moscow, opened 1973
sources: Rockefeller Archive Center chronology, rockarch.org (cited in dossier, not re-fetched)

stops.name: The Great Hall of the People, two hours with Zhou Enlai
stops.date_confidence: attested to June 1973; the Zhou Enlai meeting is confirmed by the Rockefeller University Digital Commons record, the Bank of China correspondent relationship and the August op-ed by encyclopedic biography citing the New York Times. Day not recorded.
stops.campa: He is received in the Great Hall of the People and talks with Zhou Enlai for about two hours. The visit gives Chase the first correspondent relationship any United States bank has held with the Bank of China in roughly twenty-four years. In August the New York Times prints his account of the trip under the title 'From a China Traveler,' admiring the social discipline of Mao Zedong's China, its sense of purpose and its national morale. It is written at the tail end of the Cultural Revolution. It will be quoted against him for the rest of his life.
suggested_refs: David Rockefeller, 'From a China Traveler,' The New York Times, 10 August 1973
sources: Encyclopedic biography of David Rockefeller, citing his own NYT op-ed

stops.name: Tokyo, the Trilateral Commission's first regional meeting
stops.date_confidence: founding in July 1973 and first regional meeting at Tokyo in October 1973 are attested by Wikipedia's Trilateral Commission article. Day not recorded. Richard Rockefeller's remark is quoted verbatim in Memoirs and dated there only to the 1970s at Harvard.
stops.campa: The Trilateral Commission, founded in July with Zbigniew Brzezinski as its director and Rockefeller as its principal backer, holds its first regional meeting at Tokyo in October. Three regions, one private table: North America, Western Europe, Japan. No treaty, no vote, no accountability to any electorate, and a membership list of the people who run things. His son Richard, an undergraduate at Harvard, reports back what his classmates take the thing to be. The commission is still meeting fifty years later.
stops.quote_source: Richard Rockefeller, reporting to his father what his Harvard classmates assumed of the Trilateral Commission, 1970s, quoted in David Rockefeller, Memoirs (Random House, 2002)
suggested_refs: The Trilateral Commission, founded July 1973; first regional meeting, Tokyo, October 1973

segments.name: The Shah and the End of the Chairmanship

stops.name: Belgrade, visiting Tito
stops.date_confidence: attested in substance by the Time archive piece fetched for this file, which names Tito and the Shah as objects of his travel; the article is dated 1 September 1980 and gives no year for the Belgrade visits, so 1975 is an ordering default within the decade. A dossier place-string reading 'Kyaiktiyo/Yugoslavia - Belgrade' spliced in a Burmese pagoda with no connection to the subject and is corrected to Belgrade here.
stops.campa: His travel does not slow. He calls on Josip Broz Tito in Belgrade as he calls on the Shah in Tehran, as he calls on Moscow and Peking, and the American press describes the habit without much affection. He is sixty. Yugoslavia is a communist state outside the Warsaw Pact, borrowing in Western markets, and a banker who can sit down with Tito is worth something to both sides of that arrangement. What Chase's own balance sheet is doing while he travels is a separate question, and it is being asked in New York.
stops.quote: Rockefeller appeared to be off frequently, polishing his reputation as a world statesman by visiting Yugoslavia's late President Josip Broz Tito or the Shah of Iran.
stops.quote_source: Time, 'Business: The Change at David's Bank,' 1 September 1980
suggested_refs: Time, 'Business: The Change at David's Bank,' 1 September 1980

stops.name: One Chase Manhattan Plaza, the Comptroller's list
stops.date_confidence: the regulator is corrected: the dossier said Federal Reserve, but the Time archive piece it cited attributes the 1975 criticism to the Comptroller of the Currency, who called Chase's back-office operations 'horrendous.' The article contains no mention of the Federal Reserve and none of bond-trading losses. The problem-bank listing entered the public record through a congressional leak in January 1976. Month within 1975 is an ordering default.
stops.campa: The Comptroller of the Currency calls Chase's back-office operations horrendous and puts the bank on the list of institutions requiring closer supervision. A congressional leak in January 1976 makes the listing public: Chase Manhattan, one of the largest banks in the country, a problem bank. Bad real estate loans, an operations floor that cannot reconcile itself, earnings weakened after the oil shock. The chairman is out of the country a great deal. Willard Butcher, the president, is left to clean the floor. Butcher gets the chairmanship in 1981.
suggested_refs: Comptroller of the Currency problem-bank list, disclosed by congressional leak, January 1976

stops.name: Tehran, the Shah's banker
stops.date_confidence: the visits to the Shah are attested by the Time archive piece, which gives no dates; 1976 is an ordering default inside the decade the article describes. The scale of Chase's Iranian deposits and loans is attested only in aggregate by the 1979 asset-freeze reporting. Pin is the canonical Tehran point used across the atlas.
stops.campa: He comes to Tehran to see Mohammad Reza Shah Pahlavi, whose government keeps large deposits at Chase and borrows from it, and who is a friend as well as a client. Chase handles a substantial part of the Iranian oil revenues. Rockefeller travels here as he travels everywhere, the private banker calling on the sovereign, and the American press files the visits as evidence of a man operating above ordinary commerce. By 1979 there is no Iranian government of this kind, the deposits are frozen and the loans are in litigation.
suggested_refs: Chase Manhattan's Iranian government deposits and loan book, 1970s

stops.name: New York, the visa and the embassy
stops.date_confidence: attested by Wikipedia's Iran hostage crisis article: admission to the United States for medical treatment on 22 October 1979 after Rockefeller, Kissinger, McCloy and Joseph Reed pressed U.S. officials; embassy seizure 4 November; asset freeze 14 November. The mid-1979 Mexican visa lobbying is attested in the shah's own atlas file. Pin is the canonical New York City point; the Tehran events are narrated from here because he was not there.
stops.campa: The Shah is a sick man without a country, moving between Egypt, Morocco, the Bahamas and Mexico, and Rockefeller, Henry Kissinger, John J. McCloy and the Chase executive Joseph Reed have spent months pressing Washington to let him in. On the twenty-second of October he is flown to New York Hospital for surgery. Thirteen days later students take the American embassy in Tehran and hold sixty-six people. On the fourteenth of November, with Tehran threatening to pull its money out, the United States freezes Iranian assets, and Chase's Iranian book is on the table in front of everybody.
suggested_refs: The Rockefeller-Kissinger-McCloy-Reed campaign for the Shah's admission, October 1979
Executive Order 12170, freezing Iranian assets, 14 November 1979
sources: mohammad_reza_shah_pahlavi.journey.json, the Mexico City villa stop

stops.name: One Chase Manhattan Plaza, thirty-five years ended
stops.date_confidence: retirement in 1981 with Willard C. Butcher succeeding is attested; the month is not recorded in the sources reached and defaults to April. The April 1977 South Africa lending restriction is tagged [R] in the research pool, resting on encyclopedic biography rather than a bank document. The March 2008 renaming of the plaza is attested by Wikipedia, '28 Liberty Street.'
stops.campa: He retires as chairman and chief executive after thirty-five years at the bank and hands the office to Willard C. Butcher. Four years earlier Chase had announced that it would make no further loans to the South African government or to enterprises supporting apartheid, the first major American bank to state such a restriction. He is sixty-five and has been the public face of American banking abroad for two decades. In March 2008 the plaza in front of the tower he built will be renamed David Rockefeller Plaza.
suggested_refs: 28 Liberty Street, formerly One Chase Manhattan Plaza; the plaza renamed David Rockefeller Plaza, March 2008

stops.name: Rockefeller Center, the land sold to Mitsubishi
stops.date_confidence: attested by Rockefeller Archive Center chronology: land bought from Columbia University for $400 million in 1985; 80 percent of the Rockefeller Group sold to Mitsubishi Estate in September 1989 for a reported $1.373 billion; bankruptcy 1995; reacquisition by an investor group he assembled; sold on in 2000. Day not recorded.
stops.campa: In 1985 the family and its associates bought the land under Rockefeller Center from Columbia University for four hundred million dollars. In September they sell an eighty percent interest in the Rockefeller Group to Mitsubishi Estate for a reported one billion three hundred and seventy-three million. American newspapers treat the sale as a national humiliation, Japan buying the skating rink and the Christmas tree. The Center goes bankrupt in 1995. Rockefeller assembles an investor group, takes it back, and it is sold on again in 2000.
suggested_refs: The 1989 Mitsubishi Estate purchase of 80 percent of the Rockefeller Group
sources: Encyclopedic biography of David Rockefeller, citing contemporaneous financial reporting

stops.name: Baden-Baden, the speech nobody can produce
stops.date_confidence: [R] throughout. His attendance at the 1991 Bilderberg meeting is asserted in the research dossier and was not confirmed against a Bilderberg document. The quotation attributed to him there, thanking the press for its discretion and praising supranational sovereignty, has no conference record or transcript behind it and is usually circulated spliced with an authentic, differently worded passage from Memoirs. A separate dossier claim that he attended the founding 1954 Bilderberg meeting is also unsupported: Wikipedia characterizes his Bilderberg role only as 'the only member of the Member Advisory Group.' Month is an ordering default.
stops.campa: He is placed at the Bilderberg meeting at Baden-Baden. Out of this room comes the most quoted speech he never demonstrably gave: a passage thanking the press for forty years of discretion and praising the march toward supranational sovereignty, circulated ever since as proof of everything. No conference record carries it. No transcript has surfaced. The text usually appears spliced with a genuine passage from his own book, and the forgery and the real sentence are now inseparable in circulation. Whether he was in Baden-Baden at all is asserted in one place and documented in none.
stops.quote: from the depth of something evil
stops.quote_source: Pat Robertson on the Trilateral Commission, quoted in David Rockefeller, Memoirs (Random House, 2002)
suggested_refs: The 1991 Bilderberg meeting at Baden-Baden; the unsourced 'supranational sovereignty' attribution and its circulation
sources: Research dossier myth-analysis section (attribution flagged as unverified)

stops.name: Hudson Pines, Peggy dies
stops.date_confidence: the date 26 March 1996 is tagged [R] in the research pool, sourced to Wikipedia's David Rockefeller article; the place of death is given only as New York, so Hudson Pines is the family residence pin and not an attested deathbed location. The Hudson Pines coordinate is newly separated here from Kykuit: a dossier entry gave both the identical point 41.0942, -73.859, which is wrong for Kykuit (41.0896, -73.8444) and leaves Hudson Pines, a distinct 177-acre estate north of the Kykuit park, without a point of its own.
stops.campa: Margaret McGrath Rockefeller dies on the twenty-sixth of March, fifty-five years and some months after the wedding in Westchester. She has spent the second half of her life on land conservation, on the family farms at Pocantico, and on the collection the two of them assembled picture by picture across five decades. Where she died is given in the record only as New York. He is eighty. He will live another twenty-one years in the house without her.
suggested_refs: Hudson Pines, the David Rockefeller residence north of the Kykuit park at Pocantico Hills

stops.name: The White House, the Presidential Medal of Freedom
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1998; the exact date of the ceremony is not given in the sources reached and defaults to January. The Johnson anecdote is quoted verbatim in Memoirs at the end of chapter 17, 'Engaging the Soviets,' where it carries no date at all: the only defensible dating is 1963-1969, undated, and a dossier note giving 'circa 1966-1968' is an inference, not a source. Pin is the canonical Washington point.
stops.campa: President Bill Clinton hangs the Presidential Medal of Freedom on him, for philanthropy and public service. He is eighty-three. The citation covers the museum, the university, the conservation land, the hundreds of millions given away, and says nothing about the Shah or the Trilateral Commission. He has been in this house before and on the receiving end of its irritation: Lyndon Johnson once called across a room full of union leaders to tell him what he thought of a speech Rockefeller had made in Chicago about his economic policy.
stops.quote: David, I didn't appreciate what you said about me in Chicago last week.
stops.quote_source: Lyndon B. Johnson to David Rockefeller at the White House, undated within his presidency (1963-1969), quoted in David Rockefeller, Memoirs (Random House, 2002), footnote at the end of chapter 17
suggested_refs: Presidential Medal of Freedom citation, 1998
sources: David Rockefeller, Memoirs (Random House, 2002/2003), chapter 17 footnote

stops.name: New York, Memoirs
stops.date_confidence: attested to 2002, Random House, the only full autobiography written by a member of the Rockefeller family; Open Library records six editions in English and Chinese, and no Spanish edition could be confirmed. Month of publication is not recorded in the sources reached and defaults to October. The quoted passage was located verbatim in the digitized text at archive.org rather than through secondary citations, which frequently garble it.
stops.campa: Random House publishes Memoirs, the first full autobiography any Rockefeller has written. Nelson Mandela, Kofi Annan, Henry Kissinger and John Kenneth Galbraith supply the praise on the jacket. Inside, in a chapter he calls 'Populist Paranoia,' he takes up the charge directly, quotes Congressman Larry McDonald's Rockefeller File back at itself, and answers in a sentence that will be reproduced online more often than everything else he ever wrote put together. He is eighty-seven, and he has decided to stop denying it.
stops.quote: Some even believe we are part of a secret cabal working against the best interests of the United States, characterizing my family and me as "internationalists" and of conspiring with others around the world to build a more integrated global political and economic structure, one world, if you will. If that's the charge, I stand guilty, and I am proud of it.
stops.quote_source: David Rockefeller, Memoirs (Random House, 2002/2003), chapter 'Populist Paranoia,' verified against the digitized text at archive.org/details/DavidRockefellerMemoirs2003RandomHouse
suggested_refs: David Rockefeller, Memoirs (Random House, 2002); Larry McDonald, The Rockefeller File (1975)

stops.name: Stone Barns, the farm in her memory
stops.date_confidence: attested by Wikipedia's Stone Barns Center article: 'created by David Rockefeller and his daughter Peggy Dulany as a memorial for Peggy Rockefeller, who died in 1996.' A dossier note warning that attributing the founding to David would be inaccurate inverts the record and is corrected here; the same note also fused wife and daughter into a nonexistent 'Peggy Dulany Rockefeller.' Coordinate corrected from 41.1103, -73.8371, roughly a kilometre off, to 41.1039, -73.8288. Month not recorded.
stops.campa: On the estate's agricultural land at Pocantico he and his daughter Peggy Dulany open the Stone Barns Center for Food and Agriculture, in the old dairy barns, as a memorial to his wife. It is a working farm and a school for farming, and it carries her name forward on the ground she cared about. The pasture below the barns has been Rockefeller land since his grandfather's day. Land conservation had been her own work for the second half of her life. She has been dead eight years. He is eighty-nine.
suggested_refs: Stone Barns Center for Food and Agriculture, Pocantico Hills, founded 2004
sources: Wikipedia, 'Stone Barns Center for Food and Agriculture'

stops.name: The Museum of Modern Art, the hundred million
stops.date_confidence: attested to 2005 as the museum's largest cash gift at the time; the $77 million toward the Taniguchi construction and the naming of the Peggy and David Rockefeller Building are attested by Wikipedia's MoMA article. Month not recorded.
stops.campa: He pledges a hundred million dollars to the Museum of Modern Art, the largest cash gift the museum has received. The new exhibition wing opened the year before, in Yoshio Taniguchi's rebuilding, already carries his name and his wife's: the Peggy and David Rockefeller Building. He gave seventy-seven million toward that construction. His mother helped found the museum in 1929. He has sat on this board since 1948, when he took his mother's chair. He is ninety years old.
suggested_refs: The Peggy and David Rockefeller Building, MoMA, Yoshio Taniguchi expansion, opened 2004

stops.name: Pocantico Hills, the death of Richard
stops.date_confidence: the crash of Richard Rockefeller's aircraft shortly after takeoff from Westchester County Airport is attested to 2014 by encyclopedic biography and contemporaneous reporting; the research pool gives 13 June 2014 in the geography lens. The stop is pinned at Hudson Pines rather than at the airport because the airport is where his son died, not where he was: no source reached records where David Rockefeller was standing that day.
stops.campa: On the thirteenth of June his son Richard, a physician and a former chairman of Doctors Without Borders USA, takes off from Westchester County Airport in a small aircraft he is piloting himself and comes down within minutes. Richard is fifty-eight. His father is ninety-nine, turns a hundred the following June, and has by now outlived his wife by eighteen years. Where David Rockefeller is standing when the news reaches him is not recorded anywhere.
suggested_refs: Westchester County Airport, White Plains; the crash of 13 June 2014
sources: Encyclopedic biography of David Rockefeller, corroborated by contemporaneous news reporting

stops.name: Hudson Pines, a hundred and one years
stops.date_confidence: attested by Wikipedia: died 20 March 2017 at Hudson Pines, Pocantico Hills, of congestive heart failure, in his sleep, at 101, per his spokesman. Wikipedia's Kykuit article confirms Hudson Pines as a separate property from Kykuit. The circulating story of multiple heart transplants is unconfirmed folklore: Snopes, Newsweek, People, WSJ, Time and CNBC coverage of it all blocked or returned errors on fetch, and neither English nor Simple English Wikipedia mentions any transplant.
stops.campa: He dies in his sleep at Hudson Pines, the house north of the Kykuit park where he has lived for decades, of congestive heart failure, at a hundred and one. His spokesman gives out both details. He has outlived his wife by twenty-one years, his five brothers and sisters, one of his children, the bank as he ran it, the Soviet Union and the Shah. The story that he survived seven heart transplants, repeated for years online, is supported by no record anyone has produced.
suggested_refs: Hudson Pines, Pocantico Hills, sold after his death for a reported $33 million, with sixty acres under conservation easement

stops.name: The Rockefeller family ground, north of Sleepy Hollow
stops.date_confidence: [R]. English Wikipedia's biography gives no burial location at all; the interment in the private Rockefeller cemetery at Pocantico rests on Simple English Wikipedia alone, a single lower-tier source, and no primary or news account confirming it was reached. The burial date is unrecorded and set five days after death purely to order the segment. The coordinate is corrected northward: Wikipedia's Sleepy Hollow Cemetery article places the private Rockefeller plot 'behind a high fence at the north end' of a cemetery centred on 41.0966, -73.8614, so a dossier value of 41.0906, -73.8631 sits south of the cemetery's own centre.
stops.campa: He is put in the private Rockefeller ground behind a high fence at the north end of Sleepy Hollow Cemetery, the plot reserved for descendants of his father, on land abutting the Kykuit park. The public cemetery below holds a different branch, William Rockefeller's, under a Neoclassical mausoleum of 1920 by William Welles Bosworth on a hilltop called Rockefeller Circle. There are two Rockefeller burial grounds here, with one fence between them. Where exactly within the private plot he lies is not published, and he is not listed among Sleepy Hollow's notable interments.
suggested_refs: The private Rockefeller cemetery at Pocantico Hills, reserved for descendants of John D. Rockefeller Jr.

stops.name: Christie's at Rockefeller Center, the collection dispersed
stops.date_confidence: the spring 2018 sale and the designated beneficiaries are attested by Wikipedia's David Rockefeller article; press coverage describing it as among the largest single-collection auctions on record is likewise attested there. The often-quoted total of $835,111,344 is NOT carried here: christies.com, artnews.com, theartnewspaper.com and the relevant Wikipedia list articles all failed to load, so no figure was confirmed by a page anyone here read. The exact day is an ordering default within the week of sales. Coordinate corrected from a dossier value 370 m north to Christie's at 20 Rockefeller Plaza, which is the same point as the Rockefeller Center stop.
stops.campa: Christie's disperses the Peggy and David Rockefeller collection over a week of sales at Rockefeller Center: more than fifteen hundred objects, pictures and porcelain and furniture, the contents of the houses. The proceeds are directed to Rockefeller University, Harvard, the Museum of Modern Art, the Council on Foreign Relations and the Maine Coast Heritage Trust, which is to say back into the same institutions the last seventy years were spent on. Press coverage calls it among the largest single-collection sales on record. The walls at Hudson Pines come down bare.
suggested_refs: The Collection of Peggy and David Rockefeller, Christie's New York, spring 2018
